Eurostat data stories

125 news items · 9 statistical themes · 2020–2021 · six stories revisited with today’s data

← All projects

From 2020 to 2021 I was a statistical consultant for a company contracted by Eurostat to write some articles for its “What’s New” section. I analysed the data and wrote 125 news items, on topics from migration and asylum to disability, equality and living conditions.

Many of those items used data that ended in 2018–19 or in the middle of the pandemic. Here I revisit six of them with the latest Eurostat data, and this time I make the charts myself, in R. Each case study follows the same structure: what was published → what I explored further → working with the data → design choices → code.

How I work with Eurostat data: breaks in series, flags, EU aggregates and revisions →

The six case studies

01 Environment and energy

In 2024 the EU produced 14% fewer chemicals than in 2015

What it means Output dropped sharply during the 2022–23 energy price shock and only partly recovered. Production of chemicals hazardous to health was 14% below 2015 in 2024.

What changed since my article My 2020 item used the EU-28 and 2004 as the base year. Today’s data cover the EU-27 from 2015, so the two series can’t be joined.

Line chart · env_chmhaz · Code

02 Tourism

After COVID, EU domestic tourism recovered first, but foreign grew more

What it means Domestic travel cushioned the shock and recovered first. Growth now comes from foreign visitors, who grew faster in 11 of 12 months of 2025.

What changed since my article My item covered the collapse of March–April 2020 (−93% domestic, −98% foreign nights in April). The data now show the full recovery: domestic nights were back above 2019 in July 2021, foreign nights in February 2023.

Line chart · tour_occ_nim · Code

03 Labour market

Since COVID, hybrid working has grown in all 27 EU countries

What it means Hybrid work is here to stay. Occasional homeworking rose in all 27 countries (EU 9.0% to 14.2%), while full-time homeworking fell back after its 2021 peak.

What changed since my article The 2019 figures are unchanged, but the survey changed method in 2021, so compare before and after with care.

Dumbbell chart · lfsa_ehomp · Code

04 Education and training

The EU is close to its 2030 school target, but young men are holding it back

What it means Reaching the 2030 target now depends on young men, who are above 9% in 14 of 26 countries (women in 6).

What changed since my article Figures have been revised. The EU 2020 rate went from 9.9% to 10.0%, Malta’s from 16.7% to 13.0% and Italy’s from 13.1% to 14.2%. 17 countries, not 18, were below 9% in 2020.

Scatter plot · edat_lfse_14 · Code

05 Health

Flu deaths almost vanished in the EU in 2021, then came back

What it means Pandemic measures almost stopped flu deaths in 2021. By 2023 rates had returned, at or above 2019 levels in 10 countries, so seasonal flu prevention still matters.

What changed since my article The 2016 figures are unchanged. Very low rates in some countries likely reflect how deaths are certified, not fewer flu deaths.

Heatmap · hlth_cd_asdr2 · Code

06 Digital economy and society

In 2025, only 4 EU countries had reached the 2030 digital skills target

What it means The EU rose from 54% to 60% in 2021–25. At that pace it would reach about 68% by 2030, well short of the 80% target (a simple straight-line projection).

What changed since my article The indicator was redefined in 2021, so my 2019 figures (64% for people living with children, 53% without) can’t be compared with today’s.

Progress bars · isoc_sk_dskl_i21 · Code
